GENERATE BURST T10C-hall — Run C-9 Phase 2, T10 (Matt 2026-09-29: "making a new world/scene that would fit our barbarian... It does not need to look at all like the prior painted scene"): CONCEPT PAINTING for a new game level, "THE BURNING MEAD-HALL". Art direction only: no asset is built from this image. task_id "T10C-hall".

IMAGE 1 is the barbarian's approved character sheet (identity). IMAGE 2 shows HOW HE LOOKS IN THE GAME, in full kit (conical iron helmet with nasal, mail shirt, wolf-fur mantle, bearded axe in his right hand, round red-and-cream shield on his left arm), seen from the game camera: solid sculpted forms, real light and cast shadow, a painted watercolor-and-ink surface on every part, a dark ink contour around his silhouette. IMAGE 3 is the painter's hand (a STYLE reference only, never its character).

THE LEVEL: The courtyard of a Norse chieftain's steading at night, the great mead-hall on the upper edge ablaze through its roof, sparks rising; carved dragon-head gable posts; a courtyard of trampled mud and scattered straw in the centre; iron braziers burning at the corners; a round shield wall of painted shields propped along a timber palisade on the right; a well, barrels, a toppled cart, a weapon rack; embers drifting. Lit only by fire: warm orange light pooling around each brazier and flickering from the burning hall, deep blue night beyond, strong shadows radiating away from every flame.

THE CAMERA: the game's fixed camera, looking DOWN at the ground at about 53 degrees from horizontal, three-quarter view, orthographic (no perspective convergence: parallel edges stay parallel, far things are not smaller). We see the ground plane mostly from above; the horizon, if any, only at the very top edge.
HE IS IN IT: the barbarian of IMAGES 1 and 2, in full kit, standing on the walkable ground in the middle of the scene at TRUE GAME SCALE, about one eighth of the image height, so the scene reads as a place he walks through. True human scale for everything around him: a doorway taller than him, a standing stone about twice his height.
THE LOOK, the most important instruction: the WHOLE SCENE is made the way HE is made, so that he belongs in it. Every rock, timber, stone, tree, and building is a solid sculpted form with real volume, lit by the same light as him, casting real shadows on the ground, with a painted watercolor-and-ink surface (transparent washes, hand hatching in the shade, cream paper highlights) and a dark ink contour around its silhouette. Not a flat illustration, not a photograph: a hand-painted world of solid forms under one real light, matching IMAGE 2.
Layout for play: an open walkable ground area through the middle third of the image, scenery framing it at the edges; nothing blocking the centre.
Deliver ONE 1536x1024 landscape image. No text, no labels, no interface, no border, no signature.

Two image_gen calls: variants a and b. ONE retry per variant only if the camera is not looking steeply down (a side view or eye-level view), the barbarian is missing, wrong or not in full kit, or text, labels or interface appear — name the reason. Copy outputs to out/T10C-hall_a.png and out/T10C-hall_b.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "T10C-hall"; images = the files with prompt, references (role + path) and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.

references.role: IMAGE 1 — the barbarian approved character sheet (NB-1 variant b): identity
IMAGE 2 — the barbarian as he renders in the game in full kit, 8 facings at the 52.95 deg camera (D2 swap stack 5): THE LOOK the world must match
IMAGE 3 — STYLE reference ONLY (Matt-supplied, R-C9-69): the hand
